parameters.relayBrief: research-v2 v2.0.0 — Research — derived from ACH (competing hypotheses, diagnosticity), GRADE (certainty as arithmetic), the Admiralty code (source reliability apart from item credibility), PRISMA-S (a search someone else could run), grounded theory (constant comparison, memoing, saturation) and Zettelkasten atomicity

parameters.title: Frame
parameters.instructions: State the question and the setting; declare each answer criterion as A-<n>; list the exclusions; record the prior belief; enumerate the competing hypotheses H-<n> BEFORE weighing evidence (ACH step 1)

parameters.title: Question gate
Gather
parameters.instructions: Register and freeze every source with an Admiralty reliability grade; record each search so someone else could run it; record what was found and excluded, and what was never looked at; declare the stop rule

parameters.title: Survey gate
Establish
parameters.instructions: Record each finding as it is found: one claim, evidence that resolves to a frozen source, an Admiralty credibility grade, what would refute it, and where it sits against the corpus already held. Memo as you go

parameters.title: Cold review
parameters.instructions: Apply GROUNDED (the evidence supports the claim), TOOTHED (the falsifier could actually be observed) and ATOMIC (one claim per finding — this one is judgment, not machine-checkable). Write the review; the gate runs its OWN cold reviewer over findings.json and that one decides. Your verdict is not what opens the gate, so record what you actually found rather than what you need it to say

parameters.title: Evidence gate
Challenge
parameters.instructions: Score every finding against EVERY hypothesis, mark what is non-diagnostic, and record each contradiction resolved or declared open (ACH matrix)

parameters.title: Contest gate
Conclude
parameters.instructions: Declare the calibration policy FIRST — one rule, over kinds of evidence, fixing the starting level before any conclusion is looked at — then derive each conclusion's certainty from it: its kind's starting level, one downgrade per serious concern in a named GRADE domain. Where the four-level scale absorbs a concern or every label ties, say so in floor_disclosure and name what the reader should read instead. Say which A-<n> each conclusion discharges and what would change it

parameters.title: Cold review
parameters.instructions: Review the calibration POLICY once — is one rule over kinds of evidence sound, and does its floor_disclosure say what the tied labels no longer say? — then apply DERIVED (each conclusion follows from what it cites) and CALIBRATED (the label matches the evidence) to each conclusion AGAINST that policy. The starting level and the arithmetic are settled mechanically by the gate; do not propose a different scheme, review the declared one. Write the review; the gate runs its OWN cold reviewer over conclusions.json and that one decides. Your verdict is not what opens the gate, so record what you actually found rather than what you need it to say

parameters.title: Synthesis gate
Write
parameters.instructions: Write report.md: every conclusion with its certainty, every open contradiction, every hypothesis considered, and every retrieval date

parameters.title: Report gate

checklist.judge: Read the findings in the diff and judge them yourself; you are the cold reviewer, not a grader of one. Apply GROUNDED (the recorded evidence really supports the claim, and the quoted span covers every qualifier, comparison, subject and connector the claim uses), TOOTHED (the falsifier is a concrete observation someone could make) and ATOMIC (one claim per finding). PASS only if every finding in the diff satisfies all three. FAIL and name the finding ids if any does not. Do not consider whether a review file approved them.

checklist.assert: the review carries at least 250 characters of findings

checklist.judge: Does this review apply GROUNDED (the evidence really supports the claim), TOOTHED (the falsifier is a concrete observation) and ATOMIC (one claim per finding) to the findings in the diff, by id? FAIL if it approves or rejects without naming specific items from the diff, if it makes a claim the diff does not support, if it is generic enough to apply to any artifact of this kind, or if it leaves part of the diff unjudged.

checklist.judge: Read the conclusions in the diff and judge them yourself; you are the cold reviewer, not a grader of one. For each conclusion, ask three questions. Does it follow from the findings it cites, or does it reach past them? Does the declared calibration_policy justify its starting level as a property of the KIND of evidence rather than of the claim? Is each downgrade a real concern in the domain it names? PASS only if every conclusion in the diff holds. FAIL and name the conclusion ids if any does not. The GRADE arithmetic is already checked mechanically by the gate — do not re-derive it, and do not propose a different calibration scheme. Do not consider whether a review file approved them.

FAIL if it approves or rejects without naming specific items from the diff, if it makes a claim the diff does not support, if it is generic enough to apply to any artifact of this kind, or if it leaves part of the diff unjudged.
